name: Study Template
remarks: SYNTHEA STUDY TEMPLATE MODULE
Generic patient-simulation module for OMOP observational studies using
the synthea-omop-template GitHub Template Repository.
HOW TO CUSTOMISE THIS FILE
1. Copy and rename this file to reflect your study (e.g., my_study.json).
2. Search for every REPLACE_ME token and substitute a verified concept code.
Use the concept lookup tool:
/concept-lookup <term> [Domain]          (Claude Code)
Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<term>' [Domain]  (terminal)
Tag each code [vocab query] in remarks once confirmed against the live
omop_vocab schema. Never hard-code a concept ID from training data alone.
See CLAUDE.md Rule 1.
3. Search for every RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS token and tune the numeric value
(prevalence, timing range, oversampling proportion) using literature or
institutional data for your target population.
4. Align the Covariate_N states with the covariate cohorts of the studies in consumers.yaml:
- Set each Covariate_N_Onset code to a concept in that covariate cohort's concept set (workflow/03 checks coverage).
- Set each Covariate_N_Check prevalence from your literature review.
- Change state type if domain is procedure (Procedure) or drug (MedicationOrder).
5. Set Outcome_Assessment distribution to expected outcome incidence.
6. Run workflow/03_generate_synthea_module_artifacts.R to regenerate the
visual state diagram and validate structural integrity; it also checks the module can produce the cohorts of the studies in consumers.yaml.
7. Run workflow/04_generate_synthea_csv.sh to generate synthetic CSV data.
OVERSAMPLING RATIONALE
Observational studies need more outcome events than natural prevalence
produces for robust predictive modelling. Treatment_Strategy routes 90% of
simulated patients through the index-procedure pathway by default.
Increase this proportion to enrich outcome events. Document the real-world
proportion in remarks so downstream analyses can apply calibration weights.
PLACEHOLDER LEGEND
REPLACE_ME         = concept code; fill in after [vocab query]
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS = numeric value; tune from literature or pilot data
REPLACE: <desc>    = free text; replace with your study-specific content
CLINICAL PATHWAY OVERVIEW
Phase 1  Eligibility       Age guard and onset delay
Phase 2  Diagnosis         Exposure condition onset + outpatient encounter
Phase 3  Covariates        Four comorbidity states (cover the consuming studies' covariate cohorts)
Phase 4  Treatment         Oversampling branch (non-exposed vs. target-exposed)
Phase 5  Pre-index delay   Time from diagnosis to procedure
Phase 6  Index procedure   Inpatient encounter + procedure
Phase 7  Observation       Post-discharge window (match the consuming studies' time at risk)
Phase 8  Outcome gate      Fixed-incidence branch (RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS)
Phase 9  Outcome pathway   Outcome onset, encounter, management, resolution
Entry point for every simulated patient. Transitions immediately to
Age_Guard, which holds patients below the minimum study age.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Change quantity to your study's minimum eligibility age.
Default: 18 years (most adult surgical / pharmacotherapy studies).
Guard states wait — patients are held here until the condition is true.
No OMOP record is generated by this state.
NOTE: Synthea's CLI -a flag (e.g., -a 60-100) also constrains the
starting age of generated patients. Both filters should be consistent.
Random delay after the minimum age before the patient develops the exposure
condition. Spreads cohort entry across the study period and produces a
realistic age distribution at index.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set low and high (in years) to control the age range
at cohort entry.
Default: uniform 0-30 years after age 18 → onset ages 18-48.
Example for older surgical cohort: Age_Guard quantity = 60, delay 0-30
→ onset ages 60-90.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Change quantity (default 90) to your study's upper
age eligibility limit. Patients who exceed this cap exit without procedure
records, preventing simulation of implausibly aged surgical patients.
Set to a large value (e.g., 120) to effectively disable the cap.
The underlying diagnosis that qualifies a patient for study inclusion.
This becomes the reason for the index outpatient encounter.
REPLACE_ME: Replace the code after running a vocabulary lookup.
Step 1 — identify the condition from:
the target cohort of a study in consumers.yaml (when its entry event is a condition)
or your study's phenotype definition document.
Step 2 — run the lookup:
Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<condition name>' Condition
Step 3 — replace REPLACE_ME with the verified SNOMED-CT source code.
Step 4 — update display to the concept_name from the vocabulary query.
Step 5 — tag [vocab query] in remarks.
If your index event is a procedure (domain = 'procedure'), the condition
here can represent a general indication diagnosis (e.g., osteoarthritis
before total hip replacement). Remove this state entirely if no qualifying
condition is required and route Initial → Index_Diagnosis_Encounter.
Outpatient evaluation in which the exposure condition is diagnosed and
comorbidities (covariates) are documented. This encounter stays OPEN
through all Covariate_N states and is closed at Treatment_Strategy
via Non_Exposed_Path_End or Target_Exposed_Path_End. Synthea allows
only one active encounter at a time.
REPLACE_ME: Replace the encounter code with the outpatient evaluation
type appropriate for your clinical context.
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<encounter type>' Visit
Example: Office or other outpatient visit → SNOMED-CT 185349003

codes.display: REPLACE: outpatient evaluation encounter type [vocab query]

remarks: RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set distribution 0 to the prevalence of covariate_1
in your target population. Default: 0.30 (30%).
Covariate_1 corresponds to a covariate cohort of a study in consumers.yaml
(a condition; workflow/02 lists the covariate cohorts to cover).
The concept code used in Covariate_1_Onset must map to a concept in or below
that cohort's concept set after your [vocab query]; workflow/03 checks this.
To add more covariate states: duplicate the Covariate_N_Check + Covariate_N_Onset
pair, assign sequential names, and chain them before Treatment_Strategy.
Add a covariate state only if a consuming study has a matching covariate cohort.
REPLACE_ME: Condition representing covariate_1 (domain = 'condition').
Step 1 — identify from a covariate cohort of a study in consumers.yaml.
Step 2 — run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<covariate name>' Condition
Step 3 — replace REPLACE_ME with the verified SNOMED-CT source code.
Step 4 — confirm the concept is in that cohort's concept set (workflow/03 checks it).
Step 5 — tag [vocab query] here and in the CSV file.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set distribution 0 to the prevalence of covariate_2.
Covariate_2 corresponds to a covariate cohort of a study in consumers.yaml
(a procedure; workflow/02 lists the covariate cohorts to cover).
Because the domain is 'procedure', consider changing Covariate_2_Onset
state type to 'Procedure' and adding a duration field.
REPLACE_ME: Condition (or procedure) representing covariate_2.
If the consuming covariate cohort is a procedure — if modelling a prior procedure,
change this state type to 'Procedure' and add a duration field:
'duration': { 'low': 30, 'high': 120, 'unit': 'minutes' }
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<procedure name>' Procedure
Confirm the concept is in the consuming cohort's concept set (workflow/03 checks it).
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set distribution 0 to the prevalence of covariate_3.
Covariate_3 corresponds to a covariate cohort of a study in consumers.yaml
(a drug; workflow/02 lists the covariate cohorts to cover).
Because the domain is 'drug', change Covariate_3_Onset state type to
'MedicationOrder', system to 'RxNorm', and add a dosage/duration:
'dosage': { 'amount': 1, 'frequency': 1, 'period': 1, 'unit': 'days' },
'duration': { 'low': 7, 'high': 90, 'unit': 'days' }
REPLACE_ME: Drug exposure representing covariate_3 (domain = 'drug').
Change state type to 'MedicationOrder' and system to 'RxNorm':
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<drug name>' Drug
Confirm the concept is in the consuming cohort's concept set (workflow/03 checks it).
MedicationOrder requires a paired MedicationEnd state after the delay.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set distribution 0 to the prevalence of covariate_4.
Covariate_4 is a spare covariate state: use it only if a consuming study has
a matching covariate cohort; otherwise delete the state. Name the cohort in
the study's inst/Cohorts.csv so workflow/02 lists it.
Set the state type to match the cohort's domain.
REPLACE_ME: Condition representing covariate_4.
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<covariate name>' <Domain>
Confirm the concept is in the consuming cohort's concept set (workflow/03 checks it).
Delete this state if no consuming study has a matching cohort.
Change system to 'LOINC' if domain is measurement or observation.
OVERSAMPLING DECISION POINT
Routes patients to the non-exposed pathway (no index procedure) or the
target-exposed pathway (index procedure + outcome window).
Default: 10% non-exposed / 90% target-exposed.
This is intentional aggressive oversampling to enrich outcome events.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Tune the Non_Exposed_Path_End distribution.
Increase non-exposed share → less oversampling → more realistic mix
but fewer outcome events for modelling.
Real-world proportion for this study: REPLACE with literature estimate.
Example: 'Real-world: ~40% receive medical management, ~60% procedure.'
For cohort characterisation only (no comparator or outcome modelling):
Set Non_Exposed_Path_End distribution to 0.0 and route all patients
to Target_Exposed_Path_End.
NOTE: This state also closes the outpatient encounter (Index_Diagnosis_Encounter)
via the path-end EncounterEnd states before the inpatient encounter opens.
Closes the outpatient diagnosis encounter for non-exposed patients.
These patients exit the simulation without an index procedure or outcome record.
Increase Non_Exposed_Path_End distribution in Treatment_Strategy to reduce
oversampling and produce a more representative population mix.
Closes the outpatient diagnosis encounter for patients who will receive
the index procedure. Transitions to the pre-procedure workup delay.
The inpatient encounter (Index_Admission_Encounter) opens in a later state.
Synthea requires one encounter to close before another opens.
Time between initial diagnosis encounter and index procedure. Covers
pre-operative evaluation, optimisation, and scheduling.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set low and high (in days) for your study's
typical diagnosis-to-procedure interval.
Default: 30-180 days (1-6 months) — typical elective surgical pathway.
Urgent or emergent: 0-7 days.
Scheduled outpatient procedure: 7-90 days.
Complex pre-operative optimisation: 60-365 days.
Encounter for the index procedure. The encounter class and code must
match the visit type used by the target cohort of the consuming studies.
Check the target cohort's visit criteria in each study listed in
consumers.yaml (workflow/02 lists the cohorts).
REPLACE_ME: Replace the encounter code for your admission type.
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R 'hospital admission' Visit
Inpatient: SNOMED-CT 32485007 'Hospital admission' (default)
Same-day surgery: SNOMED-CT 11429006 'Consultation'
Emergency admission: SNOMED-CT 50849002 'Emergency room admission'
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Change encounter_class to 'outpatient' if the
index procedure is performed in an ambulatory or same-day setting.

codes.display: REPLACE: inpatient admission encounter type [vocab query]

remarks: The index procedure or intervention defining target cohort membership.
This concept must map to a concept in or below the entry-event concept set of the
target cohort of every study in consumers.yaml (when the entry event is a procedure)
(workflow/03 checks this before data is generated).
REPLACE_ME: Replace code after vocabulary lookup.
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<procedure name>' Procedure
Example: Total hip replacement → SNOMED-CT 52734007
CABG → SNOMED-CT 232717009
Colonoscopy → SNOMED-CT 73761001
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set duration low/high (minutes) for your procedure.
Brief endoscopic / catheter: 30-90 min
Laparoscopic / minimally invasive: 60-180 min
Major open surgery: 120-360 min
Post-procedure observation period within the inpatient encounter.
Represents inpatient stay duration after the index procedure.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set low and high (in days).
Default: 1-7 days.
Same-day procedure (ambulatory): set both to 0.
Minor inpatient procedure: 1-3 days.
Major open surgery: 3-10 days.
Complex or high-acuity procedure: 5-21 days.
Closes the inpatient encounter after the post-procedure stay.
Patient enters the post-discharge observation window.
Outcome assessment fires at the end of Post_Discharge_Observation_Delay.
Observation window from discharge to outcome assessment.
Set to span the consuming studies' time at risk minus the
expected post-procedure inpatient stay duration.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set low and high (in days).
Default: 5-83 days. Combined with 1-7 day inpatient stay this gives
an outcome window of 6-90 days post-procedure.
30-day outcome window: high ~ 22 (+ 7 day stay = ~30 days total).
90-day outcome window: high ~ 83 (+ 7 day stay = ~90 days total).
1-year outcome window: high ~ 358.
Outcome_Assessment fires once at the end of this delay using a fixed
marginal probability. If you need time-varying or comorbidity-adjusted
incidence, replace Outcome_Assessment with a conditional_transition
that checks covariate attributes.
OUTCOME INCIDENCE GATE
Fixed-probability gate determining which patients develop the study outcome.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set the Outcome_Onset distribution to the expected
incidence in your target population (0.0-1.0). Default: 0.20 (20%).
Higher incidence → more outcome events → better model training data.
Derive from literature, pilot data, or institutional registry rates.
Examples: SSI after open surgery ~ 10-20%
VTE after joint replacement ~ 1-3%
MACE after cardiac surgery ~ 5-15%
30-day readmission after colectomy ~ 8-12%
NOTE: This is marginal (unconditional) incidence. Individual comorbidity
burden does not adjust this probability. To implement risk-stratified
incidence, replace this state with a conditional_transition tree that
checks each covariate attribute set by Covariate_N_Onset states.
The study outcome event. This concept must map to a concept in or below the
concept set of an outcome cohort of a study in consumers.yaml
(workflow/03 checks this before data is generated).
REPLACE_ME: Replace code after vocabulary lookup.
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<outcome name>' Condition
Example: Surgical site infection → SNOMED-CT 76844004
Venous thromboembolism  → SNOMED-CT 111293003
Acute MI               → SNOMED-CT 57054005
Ischaemic stroke        → SNOMED-CT 422504002
If the outcome is a procedure or measurement (not a condition), change
state type to 'Procedure' or 'Observation' respectively.
Encounter in which the outcome is diagnosed and managed.
REPLACE_ME: Replace code with the appropriate encounter type.
Follow-up visit: SNOMED-CT 390906007 'Follow-up encounter'
ED visit: SNOMED-CT 50849002 'Emergency room admission'
Inpatient readmission: SNOMED-CT 32485007 'Hospital admission'
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<encounter type>' Visit
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Change encounter_class to 'inpatient' if the outcome
requires hospital readmission (e.g., deep SSI, haemodynamically significant
PE, stroke requiring hospitalisation, acute MI).
Standard-of-care treatment for the outcome. Can be a procedure, medication,
or combination. By default this is a Procedure state.
REPLACE_ME: Replace code with the verified treatment concept.
Procedure: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<treatment>' Procedure
Medication: Change type to 'MedicationOrder', system to 'RxNorm',
and add dosage/duration fields.
Run: Rscript scripts/concept_lookup.R '<drug name>' Drug
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set duration low/high (minutes) for procedures.
Minor wound care: 30-60 min
Surgical debridement: 60-120 min
Major reoperation: 120-300 min
For medications: delete duration and add a separate Delay state after
MedicationOrder, followed by a MedicationEnd state.
To model multiple concurrent treatments, chain additional states between
Outcome_Management and Outcome_Management_Duration using direct_transition.

remarks: Duration of the outcome management episode within the encounter.
For procedure-based management: post-operative observation before discharge.
For medication-based management: course duration.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: Set low and high (in days). Default: 1-14 days.
Outpatient antibiotic course: 7-14 days.
Inpatient post-operative stay: 3-21 days.
Short observation: 0-3 days.
Closes the outcome encounter after management completes.
Transitions to Outcome_Resolution to end the condition record.
Marks resolution or end of the outcome condition.
If the outcome is chronic or lifelong (e.g., stroke with permanent deficit,
end-stage renal disease, limb loss), remove this state and route
Outcome_Encounter_End directly to Terminal.
